'''Michael Ira Rosen''' (born March 7, 1938) is an American mathematician who works on [[algebraic number theory]], arithmetic theory of function fields, and [[Arithmetic geometry|arithmetic algebraic geometry]].

==Biography==
Rosen earned a bachelor's degree from [[Brandeis University]] in 1959 and a PhD from [[Princeton University]] in 1963 under [[John Coleman Moore]] with thesis ''Representations of twisted group rings''. He is a mathematics professor at [[Brown University]].

Rosen is known for his textbooks, especially for the book with co-author Kenneth Ireland on number theory, which was inspired by ideas of [[André Weil]];<ref>for example, Weil's essay on Gaussian sums and cyclotomic fields, ''La cyclotomie jadis et naguère'', 1974</ref> this book, ''A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory'', gives an introduction to [[List of zeta functions|zeta functions]] of [[algebraic curve]]s, the [[Weil conjectures]], and the arithmetic of [[elliptic curve]]s.

For his essay ''[[Niels Henrik Abel|Niels Hendrik Abel]] and equations of the fifth degree''<ref>''American Mathematical Monthly''. volume 102, number 6, June/July 1995, pp. 495–505.</ref> Rosen received the 1999 [[Chauvenet Prize]].
